questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere where I knew I would feel home quickly. I enjoy a rainy day, and I knew the people would be kind.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, although I had to change modules because of some missing information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a dedicated introduction week for exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy to find something affordable because of the housing crisis.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It depends on where the university is located. My university were outside the city centre, and I was very happy to live off campus and more central. I  was lucky to have a lovely housemate, which is crucial.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to reply an email with my module wishes, and then the host university did the rest.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They made a webinar about it, and provided all the information on a padlet.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I got all my wishes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don’t expect that you can take modules that overlap, I made that mistake and had to change my OLA and everything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had some introduction modules outside of my subject, which were great. I had one level 4 module which I never got the hang off, since I had some exams colliding with the first few lectures followed by being sick for two weeks twice during the semester. I would therefore recommend not doing too high levels, especially if outside the main subject.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The semester is much shorter. Some mandatory tutorials. More assignments. Mid-semester exams. First I was very overwhelmed and a bit stressed about it, it felt more competitive than I was used to. But I ended up liking the structure a lot.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Oscillations and Waves,
Logic,
Why Trust Science,
Numerical Methods for PDE’s,
Methods for Physicists,
Programming with Big Data

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Oscillations and Waves, because it’s more fun than it sounds. 
Logic, because it’s interesting and relevant to everyone. 
Why Trust Science, because it’s not a common module. It’s a mix of different subjects and the structure is very different too. 
Methods for Physicists, it’s great if you like solving physics problems by hand.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None as far as I remember.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Housing prices were much higher than expected, including student accommodation. 
No books were required to purchase as all mandatory reading were available online.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Free cultural trips were available. Free fitness membership. We all had a contact person, one of the students from the host university. They hosted a a couple of parties, not free entry though.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely the free trips, although they are published very late and can therefore collide with other plans. Thus I didn’t attend any, but my friends said they were great

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend staying in Ireland and travelling around the beautiful country instead of going abroad. There are so many great hikes! And surfing is a lot of fun too.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, so many kind people. Truly a lovely country.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be yourself, because you are great. Then everything will work out.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The night life closes very early.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone is super friendly and polite.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find a place to stay before arriving.
Do some “social” modules, where you will be talking a lot during classes. That will help you make lots of different friends. 
Don’t stress about participating in all of the social activities during the introduction week, because it can be exhausting.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Buy a bike cheep on Adverts (second hand), it’s great to have.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It gave me an academic boost, a social boost and a motivational boost for my studies and life in general.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding the balance between socialising and charging my social battery.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
